interpretation: Numerical sensitivity on one frozen strong-aligned row only. Single-parameter swaps are counterfactual and may interact. This does not establish source/public fidelity, broad-domain stability, or release qualification.
protocol: At each tolerance level capture the exact merger_ringdown_22 arguments and discrete ringdown support inside the Torch numerical attachment; replay the corrected-v2 diagnostic without changing its phase or amplitude controls.

Reconstruct each emitted ringdown at whole-waveform times t>=the attachment boundary from the captured fine-query elapsed times sampled with the frozen factor 32, with the same strict elapsed<support_end cutoff. Compare complex samples and require a no-op re-evaluation.

On identical ringdown output times, start with baseline inputs and swap exactly one named input to refined; also reverse each single swap. Each other input stays at its starting level. For elapsed swap, use the other level’s captured elapsed samples and matching fine-query indices.

Quantify each single swap by its effect L2 divided by the full reconstructed baseline/refined difference L2 and by the fraction of error squared removed relative to refined. Report the vector residual after summing all baseline-origin single-swap effects as a nonadditivity measure. These fractions need not sum to one and may be negative.
Cross-check the emitted ringdown error square against the frozen v2 time-window attribution. Reproduce whole-mode SHA256 at both levels. No output here changes production or release gates.
purpose: Development-only attribution of the corrected v2 baseline/refined ringdown difference to the exact numerical-attachment boundary inputs using reconstruction and one-at-a-time swaps.
